ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Lorraine Hansberry — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Day 1 of cycle 4 of modified FOLFIRINOX: toxicity review, genetic and tumor profiling results, thromboprophylaxis, nutrition and mood

text.paragraph: Review on day 1 of cycle 4 of modified FOLFIRINOX. [S]

Ms. Hansberry returns on the first day of her fourth cycle; cycles 1 to 3 were given on schedule. After each cycle she has nausea for a day or two, controlled with olanzapine at night, and two or three loose stools on days 3 to 5, settled with loperamide. For a few days after each cycle cold drinks hurt her throat and her fingers and toes tingle in the cold, and the fingertips now tingle mildly between cycles; she can still type and do buttons. Pain is 2 out of 10 with one or two oxycodone tablets a day, and she sleeps through. She writes three mornings a week. Her stools are formed with pancrelipase and her weight is steady. Home fasting glucose readings are 110 to 130 mg/dL. She has had no bleeding or black stools since the iron. The germline panel and the tumor profile have both resulted. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1963-06-29; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 54.8 kg; blood pressure 110/70, pulse 84
Mild epigastric tenderness; port site clean
Light touch slightly reduced at the fingertips; vibration sense and reflexes normal; fine finger movements normal (grade 1 sensory neuropathy)

Epigastric pain for about two months, boring through to the back and worse after meals and lying flat, with nausea, early fullness, a loss of 5 kg (8 percent of her weight), and pale, loose stools: an upper abdominal cause such as a bleeding ulcer or a pancreatic or duodenal tumor must be found. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented collapse in pain and the account of a suspected duodenal ulcer. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic upper gastrointestinal blood loss: black stools on and off for three weeks, two near-fainting spells, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the documented account that she was told she had anemia and bleeding ulcers.

New hyperglycemia: A1c 6.6% and random glucose 132 mg/dL in a lean woman of 32 who is losing weight; new diabetes with weight loss can be the first sign of a pancreatic cancer, so it is to be confirmed and explained, not labeled type 2
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer was recorded at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.1 cm, invading the duodenum, borderline resectable (tumor contact of more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, no arterial contact), no distant spread, CA 19-9 486 U/mL after biliary drainage; on EUS-guided biopsy; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose primary site the sources record differently
S — Synthetic histology, site, stage and course; the sources say she died of cancer and differ on whether it was pancreatic, duodenal, or colonic with spread to the pancreas (R). See sources.md.
Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (pancreatogenic, type 3c): A1c 6.6% at intake and fasting glucose 141 mg/dL
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from obstruction of the pancreatic duct: pale, floating, loose stools after fatty meals and weight loss
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor; diagnosed clinically, as guidance allows in pancreatic cancer.
Cancer-related pain in the upper abdomen and back, 6 out of 10, with sleep broken by it
S — Synthetic symptom of the synthetic tumor.
Obstruction of the distal common bile duct by the tumor, relieved by a covered metal stent placed at ERCP
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.

Oxaliplatin peripheral neuropathy, grade 1: tingling in the fingers and toes in the cold, lasting a few days after each cycle, with mild tingling at the fingertips between cycles; no effect on writing or buttons
S — Synthetic common effect of oxaliplatin.

list.item:
Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, borderline resectable, on modified FOLFIRINOX (C25.0). Responding by marker: CA 19-9 210 U/mL from 486. The germline panel is negative, so there is no inherited variant to pass on and no reason for platinum or PARP inhibitor choices based on one; the tumor carries the usual KRAS G12D change with no targetable alteration, so modified FOLFIRINOX remains the right treatment. Counts, kidney and liver function allow full doses today: neutrophils 5.8 with pegfilgrastim, platelets 214, creatinine 0.72 mg/dL, bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests before cycle 1 were negative. [S]
Cycle 4 at full dose today.
Interim restaging CT in two weeks, before cycle 5.
Second recombinant zoster dose given today.

Oxaliplatin neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Grade 1 sensory neuropathy, persisting mildly between cycles. No drug prevents it; the dose is continued at grade 1 and reduced or stopped if it reaches grade 2 or affects her hands. [S]
Avoid cold drinks and use gloves for the days after each cycle.
Check before each oxaliplatin dose.

Iron deficiency anemia from blood loss (D50.0). Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL and ferritin 88 ng/mL: iron stores replaced; no bleeding for eight weeks. [S]
Blood count with each cycle.

Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (E08.9). Glucose 128 mg/dL; home fasting readings 110 to 130; no treatment needed yet. [S]
A1c with the restaging tests.

Cancer-related pain (G89.3). Controlled: 2 out of 10 on one or two oxycodone tablets a day, with a clear head. [S]
Continue; review with palliative care monthly.

A deviation: the dilated eye examination and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio planned when diabetes was diagnosed were not arranged, amid staging and the start of chemotherapy. Harm is unlikely after two months of mild diabetes, but the check is a standard of care. Corrective action: both booked with the visit after surgery, when treatment visits are fewer
At diagnosis, at each treatment phase, and when symptoms change
PHQ-9 8 and GAD-7 9; worry before scans; she sees the palliative care social worker monthly

list.item: Endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT within one week, tissue diagnosis and biliary drainage within two weeks, and a tumor board plan within three weeks of presentation. Outcome by 1963-05-04: Endoscopy in two days, CT in three, EUS biopsy and stent in one week, tumor board in nine days, consultation at two weeks [S]

Germline genetic testing with counseling and tumor molecular profiling resulted before surgery. Outcome by 1963-06-29: Germline panel negative; tumor KRAS G12D, microsatellite stable, no targetable alteration [S]
Six cycles of modified FOLFIRINOX before surgery with no delay of more than one week. In progress; target 1963-08-10 [S]
Resection with clear margins if restaging shows no progression. In progress; target 1963-10-05 [S]
Pain 3 out of 10 or less with a clear head for writing. Outcome by 1963-06-29: Pain 1 to 2 out of 10 on oxycodone 5 mg once or twice a day [S]
Weight kept within 5 percent of the weight at diagnosis through chemotherapy, with enzyme replacement and dietitian support. In progress; target 1963-08-10 [S]
PHQ-9 below 10 throughout treatment, with support she chooses and palliative care alongside cancer treatment. In progress; target 1963-10-05 [S]

Call at once for fever of 38.0 °C or more, diarrhea not controlled by loperamide, bleeding, or yellow eyes. Next scheduled visit 1963-08-10: after six cycles: restaging CT and CA 19-9, decision for surgery, and preparation for pancreaticoduodenectomy. [S]
